entry.title: Porsche x La Marzocco | Carrera RS 2.7 Collection

media:group.media:title: Porsche x La Marzocco | Carrera RS 2.7 Collection
media:group.media:description:
Porsche x La Marzocco – The 911 Carrera RS 2.7 Collection.
Two icons of precision engineering, united by a shared appreciation for great design. The Linea Micra espresso machine and Pico grinder take inspiration from the legendary Porsche 911 Carrera RS 2.7, bringing motorsport heritage into a different kind of daily ritual.
Available in two historic colourways: grandprix-white – green and tangerine. The collection features details inspired by the original, from the Carrera RS script to a cup rail shaped like the iconic ducktail. Matching espresso and cappuccino cups complete the collection.
Limited to 911 units per colourway. Available from 30 October at shop.porsche.com, select Porsche Centres and Porsche Design Stores.
Driven by a taste for excellence. Visit the Porsche RS 2.7 Collection: https://porsche.click/LaMarzocco_RS-Collection

entry.title: World Record Speed on a Skateboard | Porsche x Red Bull

media:group.media:title: World Record Speed on a Skateboard | Porsche x Red Bull
media:group.media:description:
The fastest speed ever recorded on a skateboard. 151.83 km/h.
Diego Poncelet, two-time downhill world champion, took on Les Éboulements, Quebec. 2.5 km. Steep. Curving. The same road where his friend Peter Connolly set the previous record of 146.73 km/h.
Now it’s his. A new Guinness World Records title.
Filmed from a Porsche 911 chase car.
Watch the full story on Red Bull’s channel: https://porsche.click/WR_speed_skateboard

entry.title: Porsche Mission S | Design Walkaround with Tobias Sühlmann​

media:group.media:title: Porsche Mission S | Design Walkaround with Tobias Sühlmann​
media:group.media:description:
Everything a sports car needs and nothing more.​
Tobias Sühlmann, Vice President Style Porsche, walks us around the Mission S – a glimpse into the future of sports cars, shaped by our heritage.​
Mid-engine architecture. A pronounced Porsche Flyline. A wraparound main line connecting the light signatures at the front and rear. Torpedo-style fenders. A visible fan wheel at the rear – a homage to the 917. Dial-style wheels, reinterpreted from the 928.​
Inside, a consistent focus on the driver. A central digital rev counter with an analogue needle. A height-adjustable gear lever. An aluminium key. And sports seats with motorsport DNA.​
Authentic. Consequent. Timeless.​
https://www.porsche.com/international/models/mission-s/​ ​
